ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC = \angle ABC = 42^\circ$. Through point C, draw $CD \perp AB$ at point D. Let point E be a point on $CD$. If $\triangle ACE$ is folded along $AE$ to obtain $\triangle AFE$ and points E, F, B are exactly on the same line, connect $CF$. What is the measure of $\angle CFA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Since $CD \perp AB$\\
$\therefore \angle ADC = 90^\circ$ \\
Since $\angle BAC = \angle ABC = 42^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle ACD = 90^\circ - \angle BAC = 48^\circ$, $AC = BC$\\
Since $CD \perp AB$\\
$\therefore \angle BCD = \angle ACD = 48^\circ$ \\
In $\triangle ACE$ and $\triangle BCE$\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
AC = BC\\
\angle ACD = \angle BCD\\
CE = CE
\end{array}\right.$ \\
$\therefore \triangle ACE \cong \triangle BCE$\\
$\therefore \angle CAE = \angle CBE$ \\
Since folding $\triangle ACE$ along $AE$ yields $\triangle AFE$,\\
$\therefore \angle AFE = \angle ACD = 48^\circ$, $\angle CAE = \angle FAE$, $AC=AF$\\
$\therefore \angle CAE = \angle FAE = \angle CBE$\\
Let $\angle CAE = \angle FAE = \angle CBE = x$\\
$\therefore \angle BAF = \angle BAC - \angle CAE - \angle FAE = 42^\circ - 2x$, $\angle ABF = \angle ABC - \angle CBE = 42^\circ - x$ \\
Since $\angle AFE = \angle BAF + \angle ABF = 42^\circ - 2x + (42^\circ - x) = 84^\circ - 3x$ \\
$\therefore 48^\circ = 84^\circ - 3x$\\
$\therefore x = 12^\circ$ \\
$\therefore \angle CAF = \angle CAE + \angle FAE = 24^\circ$ \\
Since $AC=AF$\\
$\therefore \angle CFA = \angle FCA = \frac{180^\circ - \angle CAF}{2} = \boxed{78^\circ}$

Because E, F, B are collinear, ∠AFE is the exterior angle at F of △ABF, therefore ∠AFE=∠BAF+∠ABF. Also ∠ABF=∠ABE=θ, so 48°=(2θ−42°)+θ=3θ−42°. Solving gives 3θ=90°, θ=30°. Image description: In the figure, AB is the horizontal base, A is on the left, B is on the right, and C is above AB; from C, draw the vertical line CD to AB, D is on AB and is marked with a right-angle symbol; E is located on CD, between C and D; the point F obtained after folding is located on the right side, in the figure E, F, B are on the same straight line, and line segments such as AE, AF, CF are drawn.

Reasoning: Because ∠BAC=∠ABC=42°, △ABC is an isosceles triangle, AC=BC. Also in the figure CD⊥AB, and CD is the altitude from the vertex C of the isosceles triangle to the base AB, so CD is also the perpendicular bisector of AB. Therefore E is on CD, so AE=BE, and △AEB is an isosceles triangle.

Let ∠BAE=∠ABE=θ. Because ∠BAC=42°, and AE is inside ∠BAC, ∠CAE=42°−θ.

Fold △ACE along AE to obtain △AFE, the crease AE remains fixed, and C maps to F, therefore ∠EAF=∠CAE=42°−θ, and AC=AF. Since in the figure AF is between AB and AE, so
∠BAF=∠BAE−∠EAF=θ−(42°−θ)=2θ−42°.

Also CD⊥AB, ∠BAC=42°, so in the right triangle ACD, ∠ACD=90°−42°=48°. Since E is on CD, ∠ACE=48°. Folding preserves angles, so ∠AFE=∠ACE=48°.

Because E, F, B are collinear, ∠AFE is the exterior angle at F of △ABF, therefore
∠AFE=∠BAF+∠ABF.
Also ∠ABF=∠ABE=θ, so
48°=(2θ−42°)+θ=3θ−42°.
Solving gives 3θ=90°, θ=30°.

Thus ∠CAE=42°−30°=12°, and ∠EAF=12°, so
∠CAF=∠CAE+∠EAF=24°.
From folding, AC=AF, therefore △ACF is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal:
∠CFA=∠FCA=(180°−24°)/2=78°.

Final answer: ∠CFA=78°.
